title: Spec prices bundle edges at the representative pipe's cost; code prices at the MIN member cost
detail: Spec says edge cost = the lowest-slot representative pipe's tier cost; code prices at the MIN member cost. They diverge when a mixed-tier bundle's lowest-slot pipe is the pricier one. Arch and decision-log agree with code — doc-accuracy note.
recommended_fix: Reword spec Changes item 2: edge cost = MINIMUM tier cost among the pair's live pipes (fattest member); the lowest-slot pipe only records Hop.pipe.

title: i32 dist accumulation can overflow: cost has no upper bound at catalog load
evidence:
+			if t.id == "" || t.capacity_units <= 0 || t.max_span <= 0 || t.cost_per_tile < 0 || t.cost < 1 {

+				nd := dist[cur] + cat.pipe_tiers[t.pipe_tier[pi]].cost
detail: `cost` is i32 with only a lower bound (>= 1); a pathological ladder value overflows the i32 `dist` accumulation in routing_rebuild, corrupting shortest paths (and can collide with the -1 UNREACHABLE sentinel). Documented in deferred-work.md; note-level per ruling.
recommended_fix: Add an upper-bound validation for pipe_tiers cost (e.g. <= 1e6) at catalog load, as deferred-work.md already proposes.

title: routing_cost_test dereferences hops[off+1] after a non-fatal count check
evidence:
+	testing.expectf(t, count == 2, "different-tier equal-sum tie must ECMP (count 2), got %d", count)
+	testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1 && s.routing.hops[int(off + 1)].node == m2,
+		"tie hops are {{m1, m2}} (insertion order), got {{%d, %d}}",
+		s.routing.hops[int(off)].node, s.routing.hops[int(off + 1)].node)
detail: expectf is non-fatal; when count != 2 the next assertion still dereferences hops[off+1] — reading the adjacent row's Hop or panicking out-of-bounds — instead of a clean pin failure. The unique-hop pins (a)/(d) share the pattern (hops[off] after count==1).
recommended_fix: Guard the node asserts with the count condition (if count == 2 / count == 1) so a routing regression fails via the expectf, not an index panic.
